questions.q: In the Asiatic cholera epidemic of 1831, the remedy Hahnemann advised for the first stage was:
questions.why: Hahnemann advised Camphor in the first stage and Cuprum or Veratrum album in the later stages of cholera.

questions.q: In the sixth edition of the Organon Hahnemann preferred the term:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Earlier editions said 'vital force' (Lebenskraft).

questions.q: Convulsions with the head bent backward (opisthotonos) and violent jerks, especially after a head injury, call for:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Cicuta: opisthotonos, ill effects of concussion.

questions.q: A fever patient who must be covered in every stage, because he becomes chilly on the slightest uncovering or movement even during the heat, needs:
questions.why: Nux vomica: chilliness in all stages of fever; cannot move or uncover without feeling chilly (Allen's Keynotes).

questions.q: A gastric ulcer that is round and 'punched out', with pain felt in a small spot, calls for:
questions.why: Kali bich has deep, round, punched-out ulcers on mucous membranes and pains in small spots that can be covered with a fingertip.

questions.q: Chest pain at rest, often in the early morning, with transient ST-segment elevation that settles with nitrates and normal troponin, is typical of:
questions.why: Variant angina results from coronary artery spasm, giving transient ST elevation at rest; pericarditis gives widespread, persistent concave ST elevation.

questions.q: Barthel and Klunker's 'Synthetic Repertory' covers mainly:
opts: Mind, Generalities, and Sleep, Dreams and Sexuality
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Three volumes of general symptoms.

questions.q: An ulcer with a punched-out edge, as if cut with a punch, is typical of a:
questions.why: Punched-out edges are seen in gummatous (and trophic) ulcers; TB is undermined, SCC everted, BCC rolled.

questions.q: Long-term corticosteroid therapy must be tapered rather than stopped abruptly because:
opts: the kidneys can no longer excrete potassium
the steroids have permanently destroyed the pituitary
negative feedback has suppressed CRH and ACTH, and the adrenal cortex has atrophied
the liver has stopped making cortisol-binding globulin
questions.why: Exogenous steroid suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis; abrupt withdrawal can cause acute adrenal insufficiency.

questions.q: Inability to pass urine in the presence of others is characteristic of:
questions.why: Natrum mur (Allen's Keynotes): cannot pass urine in the presence of others.
